page: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v5 is an ARM64 general-purpose server instance within the DPDSv5 family, powered by a 64-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a fixed 3.0 GHz clock speed. The virtual machine allocates 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing deterministic execution without thread contention. Each core features 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache, supported by a 32 MB shared L3 cache. System memory is configured at 208.0 GB, equating to a 3.25 GB per-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 2,577 GB of bundled local SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include a GPU and provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel computing capabilities alongside modest single-thread metrics. The server achieves top-quartile performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Clang software compilation, and stress-ng multi-core evaluations. In-memory data structures perform exceptionally well, evidenced by cached memory read bandwidth reaching 4,383.55 GB/s and Redis SET operations attaining 82.63 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect the limitations of the Neoverse-N1 core design, with lower results in single-core Geekbench, single-threaded compression, and text processing. Inference evaluations indicate functional speeds for smaller language models (135M to 7B), while 70B parameter models show constrained throughput.

The D64pds_v5 offers high core density and qualitative operational cost efficiency by substituting multi-threaded virtual cores with dedicated ARM silicon. The integrated 2,577 GB local SSD provides high-speed scratch space without incurring detached volume attachment overhead. Workloads reliant on single-thread clock speed or x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 represent poor alignment. The platform is best matched for parallelized compute tasks, continuous integration and build pipelines, containerized microservices, distributed cache layers, and ARM-compatible relational or key-value database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v5 is an ARM64 general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 208 GB of RAM and 2,577 GB of integrated local SSD storage without a discrete GPU. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core scalability, evident in top-tier results for Clang software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis in-memory operations exceeding 82 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded operations reflect lower baseline performance characteristic of the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Offering high core density and integrated high-speed local disk capacity, the D64pds_v5 presents an efficient architecture for concurrent, non-vectorized workloads including container orchestration clusters, distributed CI/CD build environments, web tier serving, and high-throughput database systems.
